pr.title: Theme the panel through named roles, with ink as its default
pr.head: 9dc72ffd820f5420714d8d4cf070e36779d28b33

summary: Projector's panel is the area Claude Code draws above the prompt, listing the session's pull requests and the inbox's questions and notices. Until now each element's color was a name written where the element draws it, and only the background was a setting, panel.background. A background could hide the text drawn on it, and no other color could change.

This pull request routes every color through one of thirteen named roles, such as muted for the header, ages, and hint, or question for an open question's line. Each role's default is a Claude Code theme key, a color name like subtle that Claude Code resolves differently on each of its themes, so the defaults follow dark, light, daltonized, and custom themes. The new module hooks/theme.ts owns the roles, the built-in panel themes, and a contrast check, and resolves them into one color per role.

SettingTakes
panel.themeA built-in theme: ink (the default), umber, stone, or graphite. Each is only a background, one shade for dark Claude Code themes and one for light.
panel.backgroundA theme's name, smoke, black, white, or a literal color such as rgb(30,30,40). auto and sidebar no longer work.
panel.colors.<role>A literal color, one of Claude Code's 23 public theme keys, or default for Claude Code's own text color.

The panel refuses a color that would vanish: under 1.5:1 contrast, as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2 define the ratio, against the color it draws on. To measure a theme key, it keeps a copy of Claude Code's palette for dark, light, and their daltonized themes. A role's override that would vanish gives way to the role's default, and a background that would hide a default, or Claude Code's own text, gives way to the theme's background and then to ink's. Each refusal is said once a session in a toast. The CLI learns only that the new keys hold strings.

cards.title: Where the review stands
cards.html:
• One open finding: the panel re-reads its settings after project config set panel.… runs through Bash, but not when an option such as --user comes before the key. That change then waits for the next reload, up to 30 seconds.
  • The palette copy matches Claude Code 2.1.299 and 2.1.300, whose theme values are identical.
  • The gate passes at this head: 224 hook tests, 1098 Python tests, the type check, and both plugin validations.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Role: a named meaning a color has in the panel, such as muted or branch.
  • Theme key: a color name Claude Code resolves per theme, such as subtle or permission.
  • Base: whether a Claude Code theme is dark or light; a custom theme names its base in its file.
  • Vanish: contrast under 1.5:1 against the color drawn on.
  • ANSI theme: dark-ansi or light-ansi, whose colors come from the terminal's palette, which the panel cannot see.

groups.title: The shapes the panel stores
groups.kicker: New types for the theme, the roles, and the resolved colors
intro: The panel keeps its state in atoms, small named stores the hooks module declares in hooks/types.d.ts. Three atoms replace the two background ones: panelTheme holds what the panel knows of the Claude Code theme, panelSettings holds the panel table as the CLI printed it, and panelColors holds one color per role. The types live in this file because the plugin's types contract may import nothing.

files.note: Adds Base, ClaudeCodeTheme, TextRole, and Colors, and swaps the state keys. A role absent from Colors draws in Claude Code's text color.

groups.title: The roles, themes, and contrast check
groups.kicker: hooks/theme.ts, the module that turns a theme and settings into colors
intro: resolve(theme, settings) is the heart of the change. It reads the panel table and returns one color per role plus a list of problems to toast. It builds a list of backgrounds to try, in order: panel.background, then the theme panel.theme names, then ink. On each it gives every role its override when the override would not vanish, and its default otherwise. If a default, or Claude Code's own text, would still vanish, it moves to the next background. ink always stands.

The contrast check can only measure colors it knows: literal rgb() and hex colors, ansi256(n) from 16 up through the standard xterm table, and theme keys on the four themes whose palette it holds. On an ANSI theme or an unreadable custom theme it compares names only, so a background there can still hide a role, as the plan records.

checks.text: No role's default comes within 1.5:1 of any built-in background on the four known themes; measured with contrast for every role, theme, and background. The lowest is reviewing on stone on light-daltonized, at 1.79:1.

files.note: New. Role defaults, the four built-in themes, the background aliases, Claude Code's palettes, the contrast ratio, and resolve.

checks.text: ROLE_DEFAULTS is where watching and branch moved from palette slots to remember and planMode, the theme keys nearest in hue to the old blue and cyan.
Each palette matches the theme objects in the Claude Code 2.1.299 and 2.1.300 binaries key for key; the two releases hold identical theme values. Extracted from both binaries and compared.

Claude Code draws a button's label and a link in its own text color, which no role can change, so the check compares a background with white on a dark base and black on a light one. That is what refuses white on dark.

On dark, panel.background of rgb(80,80,80), #505050, or ansi256(239) matches subtle and falls back to #100f0c with one problem; adding panel.colors.muted = rgb(200,200,200) lets both draw. Run against resolve directly.

files.note: New. Tables of contrast ratios, theme reads, and resolve cases, including fallbacks through several backgrounds.

groups.title: The CLI's new keys
groups.kicker: config.py learns panel.theme and a table of any lowercase role names
intro: project config set only writes keys it knows. This group adds panel.theme as a string and a new TABLES map whose entry panel.colors.<role> accepts any lowercase name under panel.colors. The panel owns the list of roles, so adding a role needs no CLI release; the panel itself toasts an unknown name. Reading needs no change: project config get panel already returns the merged table, and exits 1 with a null value when no file sets one.

files.note: _known_type looks a key up in SETTINGS, then matches it against each TABLES pattern. set and unset both go through it.

checks.text: A name must match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*, so panel.colors.Muted and panel.colors.muted.dark are refused with the key list.

files.note: Sets and unsets panel.theme and panel.colors.<name>, reads them back as the panel reads them, and checks the refused spellings.

groups.title: Drawing through the roles
groups.kicker: register.tsx reads the resolved colors and re-reads settings when they change
intro: Every color= in the panel's render now reads colors.<role> from the panelColors atom, and the old constants such as QUESTION_COLOR and THEME_BACKGROUNDS are gone. Two inputs feed the atom. paint runs when the session starts and when /theme changes the theme; it reads a custom theme's file and stores the theme. readSettings runs one timer tick after start, on each reload, and after the session runs project config set or unset on a panel. key through Bash. Both then call recolor, which chains each resolve after the last so a stale one never stores its colors over a newer one.

files.note: Draws every color through the roles, reads the panel table in one CLI call, and toasts each new problem once a session.

checks.text: SETS_PANEL matches only when the key follows set or unset directly. project config set --user panel.theme umber is a valid command it misses, so that change waits for the next reload, up to 30 seconds. Reproduced by putting --user first in the re-read test, which then fails.
A custom theme's file gives the base and the overrides. A base outside Claude Code's six theme names is read as unknown here, while Claude Code draws it as dark.
recolor chains on the previous promise, so resolves land in the order they started.

files.note: One test per acceptance criterion in the plan's § 4: defaults on each Claude Code theme, each setting, each refusal and its toast, and the re-read after a Bash set.
